target_profile.system_boundary: github.com/hashicorp/raft (captured snapshot commit c0dc6a0b) - a single Go module implementing the Raft consensus algorithm; the library owns election, log replication, commit advancement, membership and FSM application, while Transport, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and FSM are caller-supplied interfaces.
protocol_contexts: Leader/follower/candidate state machine driven by the rpcCh, applyCh, configurationChangeCh, verifyCh, userRestoreCh and timers of a single main goroutine
RPC contexts AppendEntries, RequestVote, RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot and TimeoutNow, gated by checkRPCHeader protocol-version negotiation
Membership contexts: at most one uncommitted configuration; voters vs non-voters vs staging
external_interfaces: FSM (fsm.go) plus the public client API in api.go
ownership: Main goroutine owns raftState.currentTerm/state, configurations, LogStore mutation order and RPC handling
commitment struct owns matchIndexes/commitIndex/startIndex under its own mutex
Replication goroutines own followerReplication.nextIndex, failures and pipeline state
selection_injection: Transport, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and FSM are injected by the caller via Config; the library does not implement them
variants: Pre-vote may be disabled (Config.PreVoteDisabled); leader lease timeout configurable; protocol versions 0-3
unknowns: Durability guarantees of concrete LogStore/StableStore implementations are the caller's responsibility and are not established by this module

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement: turn client commands into ordered log entries and advance the commit index only on a quorum of the current voter configuration.
activities.realization_summary: Leader dispatchLogs assigns (Index,Term), stores locally and notifies replicators; followers appendEntries validate PrevLog and truncate conflicting suffixes; commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex when a quorum has stored up to an index at or after the leader's startIndex; the leader applies committed entries to the FSM.
variants: LogConfiguration is only applied when protocolVersion > 2
unknowns: Sourced explanation: the pipelined append path advances only a local optimistic send index and reports matches through updateLastAppended on success, aborting to the RPC path on failure; its interaction with the FSM batch manager remains unmapped

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority: bind every action to a current term, persist the term and vote, and hand leadership over only on a quorum of votes or an explicit transfer.
activities.realization_summary: currentTerm is persisted through StableStore before use; a node grants at most one vote per term (persistVote) and rejects requests with a stale term or an unknown leader; candidates tally RequestVote responses to reach quorumSize; any higher term observed in an RPC or by a replicator forces a step down to Follower; the leader steps down if it cannot reach a quorum within LeaderLeaseTimeout.
variants: Pre-vote path when !PreVoteDisabled and not a leadership transfer; TimeoutNow forces an immediate real election
unknowns: The leadership-transfer handshake (initiateLeadershipTransfer/leadershipTransfer/timeoutNow) is only partially traced

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation: bring a lagging or restarted node back to the leader's log/snapshot state.
activities.realization_summary: A follower that cannot provide the requested PrevLog makes the leader fall back to sendLatestSnapshot/InstallSnapshot; installSnapshot restores the FSM, log and stable state and updates last snapshot/commit indexes.
unknowns: Snapshot-store compaction and the user-triggered snapshot path were not traced

activities.purpose: Configuration and participant eligibility: decide who is a voter and which server set defines the quorum.
activities.realization_summary: Configurations are carried in LogConfiguration/LogAddPeerDeprecated entries; processConfigurationLogEntry updates latest/committed configuration; hasVote/inConfiguration decide eligibility; commitment.setConfiguration rebuilds matchIndexes over voters only; a removed leader steps down.
unknowns: Staging/non-voter promotion transitions were not fully traced

activities.purpose: Decision application and consumption: apply committed entries to the FSM in index order and resolve client futures.
activities.realization_summary: Once commitIndex advances, leaderLoop collects inflight logFutures up to the committed index and processLogs sends commitTuple batches to fsmMutateCh, then sets lastApplied and responds futures; followers apply committed entries with futures=nil.
unknowns: FSM batching manager (fsm.go) apply ordering and error propagation were not traced

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support: durable stores that let a node rebuild its term, vote, log and snapshot view.
activities.realization_summary: currentTerm and last-vote are written to StableStore; log entries live in LogStore with (Index,Term) identity; lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm are cached and rebuilt from LogStore and the latest snapshot; lastSnapshotIndex/Term come from SnapshotStore metadata.
unknowns: Startup reconstruction in NewRaft is now partially read: restoreSnapshot's ordered selection, the lastApplied/lastSnapshot/lastLog updates, and the configuration scan from the adopted index are traced, and its interaction with the snapshot-list order is confirmed in scope; the recovery of F-term-vote and the remaining startup orderings are still sourced only from the store interfaces

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion: the public API and the futures that report whether an operation was committed and applied.
activities.realization_summary: Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier enqueue a logFuture on applyCh (or return an errorFuture on timeout/shutdown) and the future's Error() resolves when the entry is applied or the leadership is lost; VerifyLeader uses a quorum heartbeat check.
unknowns: Sourced conditional relationship: a logFuture from Apply/ApplyLog carries no shutdown channel, so its Error() selects only on the response channel; the main loop and Shutdown close shutdownCh without draining applyCh, so with BatchApplyCh buffering the channel a future accepted while the loop is busy can be abandoned at shutdown and the caller blocks indefinitely instead of receiving ErrRaftShutdown (see the deferred surface). Whether that pending state is reachable with a running loop is open

A faithfully failing LogStore after DeleteRange lets the node reject an otherwise valid AppendEntries that restarts at the truncated index, the deprecated-entry configuration-decode return does the same after the store call succeeded, and the same divergence makes the node refuse a RequestVote from a candidate strictly more up to date than its real log, so the vote up-to-date check is affected too. facts.meaning: A specific server has durably stored log entries whose last entry is (index, term); the leader records this for itself when it stores, and for a follower when that follower acknowledges a successful AppendEntries.

identity.server_id: configuration ServerID of the storing server
identity.index: log index of the last stored entry

facts.validity_context: Within a term. A stored suffix is not final: a higher-term leader may truncate it via DeleteRange, after which this fact no longer holds for the removed indexes.
facts.durability: Durable through the injected LogStore; the library writes before notifying replicators or acknowledging the RPC, but the concrete store's flush guarantees are caller-supplied.
facts.recovery: lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm are reconstructed from LogStore and the latest snapshot; erased suffix entries are simply absent.
unknowns: Concrete LogStore fsync semantics are external to this module

facts.meaning: The log entry at index is committed: a quorum of the current voter configuration has stored log entries up to at least that index, and the index is at or after the leader's startIndex (the first index of the leader's term).
facts.validity_context: Holds for a leader term while that leader's commitment object exists; monotonically increasing on a node, and re-derived on followers from AppendEntriesRequest.LeaderCommitIndex.
facts.durability: Not durable by itself on the leader; the durable content is the log entries held by a quorum. commitIndex is recomputed after an election.
facts.recovery: A new leader recomputes commitment with a fresh startIndex and must replicate its first term entry to a quorum before committing anything.
unknowns: The precise follower commitIndex after a snapshot install is not asserted here

facts.meaning: A node's persistent current term, and, if it has voted in that term, the candidate identity it voted for.
facts.validity_context: Per node; overwritten when the term increases. The vote is meaningful only together with its matching term.
facts.durability: Persisted through StableStore before the value is used for safety decisions (setCurrentTerm panics on failure).
facts.recovery: Read back at start: lastVoteTerm/lastVoteCand reconstruct whether a vote was already cast in a term.
unknowns: Recovery ordering relative to LogStore at NewRaft is not traced in this map

facts.meaning: A node holds leadership for the current term: it obtained a quorum of votes (or pre-votes) from the latest configuration's voters, or was handed leadership by a transfer.

identity.term: term for which leadership was won

facts.validity_context: Only within the term in which it was won; invalidated by observing a higher term or by failing the leader lease.
facts.durability: Not durable; leadership is re-derived only by a new election after restart.
facts.recovery: After restart the node starts as Follower and must campaign again.
unknowns: How leadership transfer interacts with the persisted vote is not asserted

facts.meaning: The result of SnapshotStore.List is ordered newest-first by applied index, so the first element is the snapshot with the highest Index, as the interface documents.

identity.store: snapshot store instance whose directories were read

facts.validity_context: Holds for the list returned from a given store state; retention may omit older snapshots, and the ordering is recomputed on each call.
facts.durability: Derived from the stored snapshot metadata files; nothing is persisted by the listing itself.
facts.recovery: Recomputed on each List call from the snapshot directories and their metadata.
unknowns: Whether the term-first comparator is intended as authority ordering rather than index recency, in which case only the interface wording disagrees

surfaces.reason: The transfer is explained from source: leadershipTransfer waits until the target's nextIndex passes the leader's last index before sending TimeoutNow, leaderLoop rejects client applies while leadershipTransferInProgress is set, and the provoked election still passes the vote handler's membership, suffrage, one-vote-per-term and log up-to-dateness checks, so a non-voter or removed node cannot win. A replayed TimeoutNow cannot be distinguished because the request carries no term; that residual is recorded.

The user-triggered restore path is now traced as B-restore-abort: it aborts inflight futures with ErrAbortedByRestore before the fallible snapshot creation, sets lastLog/lastApplied/lastSnapshot to the burned index on success, and its documented 'write effectively failed' meaning is contradicted by a failed restore (confirmed in scope by an executed direct check).

VerifyLeader is a read-leadership duty explained from source: it counts the local vote, registers the future with every replicator, and is satisfied only by a quorum of voters acknowledging the leader's term through a successful AppendEntries or heartbeat; a negative answer makes the leader step down and the future fails with ErrNotLeader, and an unverifiable period ends through the lease check whose step-down cleanup answers the remaining verify futures with ErrLeadershipLost.

The pipeline is explained from source: it only advances a local optimistic nextIdx while s.nextIndex and the commitment move solely through updateLastAppended on a successful response, so a failed or stale response aborts the pipeline and the RPC path resumes from the last acknowledged index; when the next log cannot be read the send stops and the RPC path falls back to a snapshot install.
Membership-change admission and configuration log appending are mapped to the configuration/eligibility behavior.
RPC dispatch and protocol-version admission gate the AppendEntries and vote handlers already mapped.

surfaces.entry_point: Raft.Restore error reporting after a completed restore
surfaces.reason: Raft.Restore returns the confirmation no-op's error, so a leadership loss or enqueue timeout that prevents the no-op from committing is reported the same way as a restore that failed before replacing the FSM, while the applied state and burned index have already changed; the docs say only that the call blocks 'until the restore is complete or an error occurs'. Recorded as an unmapped reporting responsibility: whether the two cases should be distinguished, and whether callers rely on the current single error when deciding to re-issue, are not established.

A logFuture returned by Apply/ApplyLog is initialized without a shutdown channel, so its Error() selects only on the response channel, while the main run loop exits when shutdownCh closes without draining applyCh and Shutdown answers no already-enqueued futures. With Config.BatchApplyCh buffering the channel, a future accepted while the loop is occupied can be abandoned at shutdown and the caller blocks indefinitely instead of receiving ErrRaftShutdown. Recorded as an unmapped client-completion responsibility: whether that pending state is reachable with a running loop, and whether indefinite blocking is intended for this path, are not established.

formation.explanation: A client command enters the leader's applyCh (B-apply-api) and is dispatched by the leader main loop (B-leader-dispatch), which assigns (Index,Term), stores it in the local LogStore, marks its own matchIndex and notifies replicators. Followers accept entries through AppendEntries only after the PrevLog identity matches and truncate conflicting suffixes (B-follower-append). Whenever any server reports that it has stored up to an index, commitment.match/recalculate raises commitIndex to the quorum median once it is at or beyond the leader's startIndex (B-quorum-commit, B-commit-term-rule). The leader then applies committed entries in index order to the FSM and resolves client futures (B-leader-apply).

context.explanation: Authority is a per-term value. Each node persists its current term and any vote through StableStore before acting (B-term-vote-persist). A follower whose heartbeat timer expires starts a candidate campaign, soliciting votes or pre-votes from voters of the latest configuration and winning at quorumSize (B-election); the winner's leadership is the context in which log dispatch is legal. Context is lost whenever a higher term is observed in any RPC or replication response (B-authority-loss) or when the leader fails its lease check (B-leader-lease); both transitions clear the known leader and invalidate the previous term's leadership.

connection.explanation: The two core lines meet at the startIndex rule and at the voter set. A leader may only advance commitIndex once a quorum of the current configuration has stored the first entry of the leader's term (B-commit-term-rule over B-quorum-commit), so formation is gated by current-term authority. Conversely, authority is defined over the voter configuration (B-election, B-config-eligibility), and losing authority (B-authority-loss) aborts pending formation work: runLeader's deferred cleanup answers inflight futures with ErrLeadershipLost while the durable log prefix and the already-applied FSM state remain. Established decisions from earlier terms persist as log entries but cannot be committed by a new leader until its own term entry is quorum-matched.

open_details: The FSM batch manager is an unmapped alternative mechanism for the same facts.

Startup reconstruction in NewRaft is only partially read: the snapshot selection and the configuration scan are traced and their interaction with the snapshot-list order is confirmed, but recovery of F-term-vote across restart and the remaining startup orderings are still sourced only from the store interfaces.
A replayed TimeoutNow cannot be distinguished from a fresh one because TimeoutNowRequest carries no term; the leadership-transfer guards are otherwise explained, but this residual is not settled.
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships and their connection are grounded in read source: formation/advancement (leader dispatch, follower append, quorum commitment, application) and context/authority (term and vote persistence, election, authority loss, lease). The connection is the startIndex gate on commitment and the voter-set basis for quorum plus the ErrLeadershipLost cleanup on step down. Local anomalies (pipeline path, transfer path, snapshot restore) are retained as open details and surfaces rather than claimed as resolved.
